title: Patient Payment Plan Enrollment: Tier Fit, Hardship Determinations and Enrollment Channels
content:
**Training questions for Patient Services representatives — setting up a Patient Payment Plan**

**What is the enrolled balance, and how does it select a tier?**
The enrolled balance is the open amount of the charges selected for the Patient Payment Plan. It must fall between the smallest enrolled balance and the largest enrolled balance of the tier. When the enrolled balance fits more than one tier, the patient picks the term.

**What does the Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan need?**
A Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan needs an approved Patient Hardship Discount Program determination that has not expired on the enrollment date. That determination is required exactly where the tier requires a hardship determination. The evidence is the Patient Hardship Discount Program record of that determination — its status and its expiry date — identified by the determination's own reference, as it stands before the plan is set up.

**Is a credit check run?**
No credit check is run where the tier does not call for one.

**Through which channels may a patient enroll?**
Enrollment through the patient portal is accepted only where the tier allows patient portal self-enrollment; other tiers are enrolled by phone or at the front desk.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical cases)

| Case | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| Selected charges have an open amount that lies inside the bands of two tiers | The balance fits both; the patient picks the term |
| Selected charges have an open amount below the smallest enrolled balance of a tier | That tier cannot take the balance |
| A patient asks for the Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan holding a Patient Hardship Discount Program application that is still pending | No approved determination exists; the hardship tier's requirement is not met |
| A patient asks for the Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan holding an approved determination that expired before the enrollment date | The determination has expired on the enrollment date; the requirement is not met |
| A patient tries to enroll through the portal in a tier that does not allow portal self-enrollment | Not accepted through the portal; that tier is enrolled by phone or at the front desk |
